in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, he's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex.

To continue assessing your eligibility, could you tell me: are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, does he live with you, or do you pay towards his upbringing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home. I take care of him full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful to know.

Could you tell me where you live? Specifically, are you resident in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, no - I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Are you or your partner (if you have one) either:
- Working abroad for the UK government, or
- A member of the UK armed forces stationed overseas?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of those apply to me. I'm not working for the UK government and I'm not in the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

One more question about your situation: were you previously living in the UK before moving abroad? And if so, are you currently receiving any UK benefits such as certain types of pension or bereavement benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any UK benefits like pensions or bereavement benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

**For Alex:** To claim Child Benefit, you generally need to be living in the United Kingdom. While there are some exceptions for people living abroad—such as those working for the UK government overseas, members of the UK armed forces, or those receiving certain UK benefits like state pension or bereavement benefits—none of these exceptions apply to your situation.

**In summary:** Since you are living abroad and don't fall under any of the qualifying exceptions, you would not be able to claim Child Benefit at this time.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you return to live in the UK—you may wish to check your eligibility again at that point.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
